laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In written Afrikaans the subordinating conjunction is 'totdat'; 'tot' as a conjunction is colloquial.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'tot' is standard Afrikaans as a conjunction and reads naturally here, so 'totdat' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: met hulle in die graf gesit
laat_vaar_vorige.na: met hulle in hul grafte gesit
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The subject is plural (earlier pharaohs), so the singular 'die graf' reads as one shared grave; 'hul grafte' matches the plural.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The distributive singular 'in die graf' after a plural subject is natural Afrikaans and reads as each pharaoh's own grave, so the proposal is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: maar nie almal vir farao's nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: maar nie almal was vir farao's nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The elliptical clause lacks a verb and reads clipped; adding 'was' makes it a complete, natural clause for Grade 5.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The elliptical 'maar nie almal vir farao's nie' is natural, easy Afrikaans, and adding 'was' brings a tense mismatch with the present 'Daar is'.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: voorwerpe gevind met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun).
laat_vaar_vorige.na: voorwerpe met die naam van farao Toetankamen (in Engels: Tutankhamun) gevind.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Afrikaans places the past participle at the end of the clause; 'gevind met die naam van' is English word order. Protected names stay intact.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Placing a long prepositional phrase after the participle is accepted Afrikaans, and the proposal pushes 'gevind' behind the name and its English bracket, which is harder for a Grade 5 reader.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Hul' is the usual written possessive form; 'hulle' as possessive is more spoken.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Possessive 'hulle' is standard written Afrikaans, so swapping it for 'hul' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: om die kosbare goed te steel
laat_vaar_vorige.na: om die kosbare goed daarin te steel
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The definite 'die kosbare goed' has nothing to refer back to when the entry is read alone; 'daarin' ties it to the grave, as 'daaruit' does in the plunder entry.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The grave is named in the same sentence, so 'die kosbare goed' already refers clearly even read alone; 'daarin' only lengthens a glossary definition that should change only through the writer.
